changelog: Insert a new core principle addressing the primary finding: mark cuts that leave short subject/NP or clause fragments without predicate/auxiliary/negation/complement as high contradiction risk and rank them low.
Paraphrased C2 to a shorter wording that preserves the finding about short pre-cut fragments raising contradiction risk (addresses finding 1).
Paraphrased C4 to a shorter wording that preserves the finding about cuts that split heads from required complements reducing cohesion (addresses finding 2).
Deleted example E8 to recover prompt length headroom so core-principle edits can fit within the budget (removes a large, low-priority example that did not add new guidance for the two findings).
Replaced E1 with measured example en_us_1570 to teach the scorer that short pre-cut subject/fragments raise contradiction risk (addresses the primary finding).
Replaced E2 with measured example en_us_87 to reinforce that isolating brief determiners/subjects before a cut can produce misleading fragments and should be ranked low.
Replaced E3 with measured example en_us_455 to show harms from cutting between heads (prepositions/nouns) and their complements, teaching cohesion loss.
Replaced E4 with measured example en_us_360 to illustrate splitting verb/complement and noun-modifier relations that reduce joined translation quality.
Insert a new core principle after C2 to address the primary finding: explicitly forbid cuts that separate heads from required complements because they reduce cohesion; rank such cuts lower.
